historic/u3e1/fort-pitt-plan.jpg.description: 1759 plan of Fort Pitt, where British officers distributed smallpox-infected blankets in 1763.

historic/u3e1/royal-proclamation-1763-do.description: Printed text of the Royal Proclamation of 1763 establishing British administration, reserving lands west of the Appalachians for Native nations and requiring license for trade - London's triage to avoid another costly frontier war.

historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..description: Portrait of George Grenville (1712-1770) by William Hoare, 1764. Prime Minister 1763-1765, author of the Stamp Act.
historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..fallback_note: Wikimedia Special:FilePath -> direct upload.wikimedia.org -> NYPL (different host) -> Commons redirect
historic/u3e1/george-grenville-portrait..used_for: George Grenville intro (t04-t05), his "brutally simple" math

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-map.jpg.description: Map showing the Proclamation Line of 1763 running along the Appalachian Mountains. German-labeled version; the red line is the visual point.
historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-map.jpg.used_for: Proclamation Line of 1763 - the line along Appalachians

historic/u3e1/french-indian-war.jpg.description: George Washington at the Battle of the Monongahela (1755) — the costly war that left Britain deeply in debt.
historic/u3e1/french-indian-war.jpg.used_for: French and Indian War debt, "won the war and emptied the treasury"

historic/u3e1/proclamation-line-1763-map.description: Thomas Kitchin 1763 map 'A new map of the British Dominions in North America' showing limits settled by Proclamation October 7th 1763 - the Appalachian crest line that was to be the fence and Indian Reserve.

historic/u3e1/paxton-boys.jpg.description: The Paxton Boys marching on Philadelphia, 1764, after their 1763 attacks on Conestoga Indians.

historic/u3e1/edmund-burke.jpg.description: Edmund Burke, who coined the phrase 'salutary neglect' in his 1775 speech on conciliation with America.

historic/u3e1/chief-pontiac-portrait.jpg.description: Portrait of Pontiac, Ottawa war chief around the Great Lakes who organized the 1763 pan-Indian alliance after the French defeat, distinct from Delaware prophet Neolin whose vision urged rejecting guns, alcohol, and infighting.

historic/u3e1/jeffrey-amherst-1785.jpg.description: Portrait of General Jeffrey Amherst by Thomas Gainsborough 1785 - ordered end of French gift diplomacy and cut off ceremonies, trigger for Pontiac's alliance, associated with smallpox blanket orders.

historic/u3e1/thomas-gage-1768.jpg.description: Portrait of General Thomas Gage by John Singleton Copley c.1768, commander-in-chief who replaced Amherst August 1763 and broke Pontiac's siege campaign.

historic/u3e1/edmund-burke-1769.jpg.description: Portrait of Edmund Burke by studio of Sir Joshua Reynolds c.1767-1769, who coined term 'salutary neglect' in 1775 speech looking back at century of loose enforcement ended in 1763.

historic/u3e1/siege-of-fort-detroit-1763.description: Contemporary illustration 'Siege of Fort Detroit' - first target of Pontiac's alliance May 1763, shows how French forts became symbols of British occupation after gift diplomacy ended.

historic/u3e1/death-of-wolfe-west-1770.j.description: Benjamin West, 'The Death of General Wolfe' (1770): Wolfe dying at Quebec, 1759, the emblem of Britain's victory in the Seven Years' War.
